messages.author: 874d1671aecc5054
messages.subject: Bessel I function for Von Mises distribution
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to implement the Von Mises distribution in nimble. The PDF calls the Bessel I function, which is not available in nimble. I see from section 5.2.5 of the user manual that the Bessel K function is available as .Internal(besselK). How can I do the same thing for Bessel I? 

Thanks! 

Simona

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Bessel I function for Von Mises distribution
parts:
Assuming it is not simple to implement as a nimbleFunction, the absolute fastest way would be to use nimbleRcall to call the besselI function in R from compiled nimble.  If the documentation on that leaves you stuck, please ask more.  If you get it working but need to avoid the overhead of calling the R evaluator, you could potentially set up a nimbleExternalCall to call via C.
-Perry

parts:
Solved -- we set up a nimbleExternalCall for the C version of bessel I called by R's besselI() function (instead of the one from the GNU Library). The function is available in the Rmath library (Rmath.h file, search "bessel_i"). 

The nimbleExternalCall i set up as follows:

sink('besselI.h')

cat('
extern "C" {
 double bessel_I_internal(double x, double alpha,  double expo);
}
')

sink()

sink('besselI.cpp') 

cat('
 #include <Rmath.h>
 #include "besselI.h"
 double bessel_I_internal(double x, double alpha, double expo) {
   double ans = Rf_bessel_i(x, alpha, expo);
   return(ans);
 }
')

sink()

system2("R", c("CMD", "SHLIB", "besselI.cpp")) ## Ignore the .so (or .DLL).  We will use the besselI.o

RbesselI <- nimbleExternalCall(function(x = double(), alpha = double(), expo = double()){},
                               Cfun =  'bessel_I_internal',
                               headerFile = 'besselI.h', ## see note about paths belos
                               returnType = double(),
                               oFile = 'besselI.o')

## Check if it works by compiling it as a stand-alone nimbleFunction
cRbesselI <- compileNimble(RbesselI, dirName = ".")

cRbesselI(3, -.2, 2) ## According to besselI source code, the besselI C function in Rmath uses 1 = FALSE, 2 = TRUE in the last argument
besselI(3, -.2, TRUE) ## Matches above

## Write a nimbleFunction to wrap call to RbesselI for use in a model 
besselI_in_model <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(), alpha = double(), expo = double()) {
    ans <- RbesselI(x, alpha, 1 + (expo != 0)) ## handling of expo mimics besselI in R
    return(ans)
    returnType(double())
  })

## Use it in a model
demoCode <- nimbleCode({
  x ~ dunif(0, 10)
  nu ~ dunif(-1, 0)
  z <- besselI_in_model(x, nu, expo = TRUE)
})

demoModel <- nimbleModel(demoCode, inits = list(x = 3, nu = -.2),
                         check = FALSE, calculate = FALSE) ## Can't calculate in R with a nimbleExternalCall

CdemoModel <- compileNimble(demoModel, dirName = ".")

CdemoModel$z
CdemoModel$calculate("z")
CdemoModel$z

## A note about paths.  I recommend something like headerFile = normalizePath(file.path(getwd(), 'besselI.h'))
##  and similar for oFile.
## This is important when compiling the model, which is not by default done in your local directory.
## An alternative, which I've used above, is to give local paths to hearderFile and oFile
##   and then use dirName = "." in compileNimble for the model, which makes it use your local directory
##   for the C++ files.
## On my system, this avoided problems with a space in getwd() due to "Google Drive", but those are 
##   just OS details.

Thanks a lot for your help with this, Perry!
